messages:
jin: Heads-up — seen a 20–30% tail-latency regression on the replay harness vs our synthetic generator this morning. Repro steps and initial notes below.

sam: Hmm, which workload? long-seq or short-seq?

jin: Short sequences (<=128) but high QPS. Using the replay harness that replays prod TCP traces. Synthetic load (our old generator) doesn't show the regression.

kevin: Could be connection churn / TLS handshake overhead. Replay uses real client sockets (many short lived) while synthetic often multiplexes.

maria: Also check KV cache warmup. Replay preserves user prefixes so KV hit rate is lower at start if sessions are ephemeral.

jin: Good point. Attached quick profiler snapshot: CPU shows spikes in the kernel-selection path and a fallback to the int8-emulation kernel at tail moments.

sam: Did we hit a quantization fallback? That could increase CPU and block the CUDA queue, choking throughput.

jin: Looks like an alignment/seqLen mismatch triggers the fallback. Kernel chooser picks the fast fused kernel for seq=64, but when partial-prefetch occurs it falls back.

kevin: That interacts badly with batching heuristics. If many short requests arrive interleaved, the batcher groups them but the runtime then reshuffles which kernel to pick. If one request forces a slower kernel the whole batch suffers.

maria: For replay vs synthetic: synthetic pads requests to fixed shapes so kernel selection is stable. Replay has natural variance — hence the apples-to-apples problem.

jin: Repro snippet we used (simplified):
```
# replay harness launcher
replay_run --trace /traces/2026-03-18.bin --clients 500 --rps 2000 --keepalive=off
```
Switching to keepalive=on drops the tail by ~15%.

ops-bot: perf-dashboard: https://perf.internal/redwood/runtime/compare?run=A&run=B

sam: Important networking note: our HTTP client tests used short-lived TCP connections without TCP_NODELAY set so Nagle + TLS coalescing added extra packetization delay. For small payloads that shows up as added tail ms.

kevin: If clients create lots of ephemeral TLS sockets, the TLS handshake CPU on the host and lock contention in the kernel can spike under pressure. Use pooled connections or HTTP/2 multiplexing for synthetic to match replay.

maria: We should add a deterministic client mode that mimics the connection behavior in the replay harness (ephemeral v.s persistent) so we can do apples-to-apples. Right now we only toggle payload shapes.

jin: Agreed. Also trying a quick experiment: forced keepalive + pre-warmed socket pool + `TCP_NODELAY=1` on client side -> latency stabilizes and kernel selection fallback frequency drops (likely because batches are fuller and aligned).

sam: Another angle: batching heuristics. We could bias the batcher to avoid mixing seq lengths during an active batch window. Add a quick heuristic: only co-batch requests if seqLen difference <= 16.

kevin: That helps kernel stability but might reduce fill rate. Need cost model: tradeoff fill-rate vs kernel penalty. We can simulate with replay traces to quantify.

maria: KV cache behavior: ephemeral sessions produce cold KV caches, causing repeated prefix recompute and extra memcpys. On the profiler I saw spikes in KV lookup locks when churn high.

jin: Action items:
- sam: add deterministic connection-mode option to synthetic generator (ephemeral/persistent, keepalive/no-keepalive, tcp_nodelay toggle)
- kevin: instrument kernel-chooser to log fallback reasons (alignment/quantization/other) during replay runs
- maria: collect per-request KV-hit histograms and correlate with tail spikes
- me (jin): run a controlled sweep of batcher heuristics (seq-delta threshold) against the replay traces

sam: I'll pick up the generator patch. Quick patch plan: expose `--conn-mode {pooled,ephemeral}` plus `--tcp-nodelay` and `--http2` flags.

ops-bot: ci-run queued: runtime/replay-compare/2149001234/step-1

kevin: FYI a short-term mitigation we can flip in prod: enable an extra kernel-compat check that rejects mixed-kernel batches and forces split batches. Cheap to flip, helps tails.

maria: Longer term, we should teach the batcher a cost model (expected kernel delta penalty) so it makes smarter grouping choices.

jin: Thanks all. Let's keep the thread for quick updates — paste profiler snippets here. If anyone finds an obvious client-side test that reproduces the high tails with a single worker, call it out. :eyes:

sam: starting the generator patch now, will post PR link when ready. :hammer_and_wrench:
